Our Kenmore 80 series dryer would continue to run despite the door being open, causing clothes to tumble out.

Lifted the dryer lid to find that I could probably just replace this harness. Looked the part up on amazon to find this wonderful replacement.

If you open the dryer door and look at the switch itself, two Phillips screws hold the switch assembly in place. I removed them and disconnected the switch’s wire harness.

I was too lazy to grab a flathead or another tool, so I used a knife to act as a flathead to free the switch’s wire harness from where it connects to the rest of the dryer’s harness.

Popped the new assembly into place, screwed the two Phillips head screws in, and connected the wire harnesses.

Total time for job: 60 seconds
Tools used: Phillips screwdriver and flathead (or similar tool)

I have no idea how much I would have had to pay a repair person to come and diagnose and fix the problem when my clothes dryer stopped working, but I'm sure the charge would NOT have been under tend dollars. However, my housemate (who does most of the laundry anyway) checked out dryer problems on youtube, figured out what part we needed, and found it on Amazon. Although it took a couple of days to get here, it arrived, was installed in no time, and we are back in business - incidentally, the light inside the dryer (which went out years ago) is fixed now, also! Three cheers for YouTube and Amazon!

Tools Required-1-Philips Screw Driver 2-Putty Knife (Stiff one is preferable, but flexible one can work too). Good videos for various dryers on Youtube. My mother's 12 year old Kenmore Dryer wouldn't start & light wouldn't go on when opened the dryer door. One sibling suggested getting a new dryer, but I knew prior that the switch was going as I had an issue with the light not going on when I opened the door a few months ago. Besides, I like the old dryer without all the fancy circuit control boards that, from what I hear from others, go bad way too soon requiring an expensive repair.

The hardest parts were 1-getting the dryer vent hose reconnected to the wall vent at the bottom of the wall when I was finished (terrible design on running of house duct) & 2-popping the top panel off this dryer with the putty knife as it seemed to be on there pretty good although it's only held on by 2 hidden plastic clips at the front beside the 2 screws in the lint filter housing. Plugged my model # into youtube search &, sure enough, videos for this common repair popped up. I bought 2 since I anticipate it happening again a few years down the road, if not sooner, & it's an inexpensive, small item to store near the dryer.
